rationale: Evidence from the last race (iteration 4, ki 0.60) scored 103.99, below the ki 0.30 design at 140.28. Oval finishes fell from 3 to 1 of 20, and oval line-loss events rose from 1.7 to 1.85. The s-bend was unchanged at 2.0 line losses and max_error 0.061. The integral increase did not help the drift and cost finishes, so the Evaluator's suggestion to try ki 1.0 is rejected. I keep ki 0.30, which is the best raced integral setting. Line losses (1.7 on the oval, 2.0 on the s-bend) are the main remaining failure, and max_error (0.061 to 0.063 m) just exceeds the 0.06 m floor. The earlier spread change (x = ±0.012 to ±0.024 m) cut line losses and raised the score, so I widen the spread once more to x = ±0.032 m. The outer sensors then see the tape at larger offsets and give earlier warning before all sensors lose it. The weights stay antisymmetric at (-1.6, -0.8, 0, 0.8, 1.6), so the signal scale is unchanged. kp 3.0, kd 0.30, ki 0.30, base_speed 1.5, footprint 0.016 m and last_direction are all kept, so this is a single-variable change from the best design. Expected result: line_loss_events fall on the s-bend and oval, max_error drops toward or below 0.06, and the oval finish count stays at 3 or rises. Risk: a wider spread may lower the sensitivity near centre and add oscillation. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.25, the next step is kd 0.40. Hypotheses: H1, line losses come from sensors losing the tape at offsets around 0.04 m, which wider spread covers. H2, the steady drift is not an integral bias, since ki 0.60 did not reduce it. Measurements wanted: line-loss timing (bend or straight), max_error location on each track, steering_oscillation, and oval completion_time.
